question: From what date do the high-risk requirements apply to AI systems listed in Annex III?
reference: From 2 December 2027. Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i), as amended, makes Chapter III, Sections 1 to 3 (except Article 6(5)) apply from that date to systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(2) and Annex III.
probe: the original text said 2 August 2026; a stale corpus answers with that date
evidence: 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III

question: From what date do the high-risk requirements apply to AI systems that are high-risk because they are safety components of products covered by the Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I?
reference: From 2 August 2028. Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(ii), as amended, covers systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(1) and Annex I.
probe: the original text said 2 August 2027 for Article 6(1)
evidence: 2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I

question: Is it prohibited to place on the market an AI system that generates realistic sexually explicit images of an identifiable person without that person's consent?
reference: Yes. Article 5(1), first subparagraph, point (ba) prohibits placing on the market, putting into service or using an AI system that generates or manipulates realistic images, videos, audio or similar material of an identifiable natural person's intimate parts, or of that person engaged in sexually explicit activities, without their freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent. Under Article 5(1a) placing on the market is only prohibited where that generation is the intended purpose, or a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without reasonable and adequate safeguards.
probe: new prohibition; the original Article 5 has no such point
evidence: generates or manipulates realistic images, videos, audio or similar material of an identifiable natural person's intimate parts

question: From when does the prohibition on AI systems that generate non-consensual intimate images of identifiable people apply?
reference: From 2 December 2026. The prohibition is Article 5(1), first subparagraph, point (ba), and Article 113, third paragraph, point (a), as amended, keeps Chapters I and II at 2 February 2025 except points (ba) and (bb) and Article 5(1a) and (1b), which apply from 2 December 2026.
probe: needs the prohibition and the date carve-out; a stale corpus can only offer 2 February 2025
evidence: of an identifiable natural person's intimate parts
points (ba) and (bb), and Article 5(1a) and (1b) which shall apply from 2 December 2026

question: Does the AI literacy obligation require providers and deployers to guarantee a particular level of AI literacy among their staff?
reference: No. Article 4(1), as replaced, requires providers and deployers to take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf, and states that the obligation does not require them to guarantee any specific level of AI literacy of any individual.
probe: the original Article 4 required measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy
evidence: This obligation does not require providers or deployers to guarantee any specific level of AI literacy of any individual.

question: Can a deployer of a high-risk AI system process special categories of personal data to detect and correct bias?
reference: Yes, exceptionally. Article 4a(2) allows deployers of high-risk AI systems (and providers and deployers of other AI systems and models) to process special categories of personal data where strictly necessary for bias detection and correction and where all the conditions and safeguards in Article 4a(1) are applied. It does not create an obligation to carry out such bias detection.
probe: the original basis, Article 10(5), covered providers of high-risk systems only and has been deleted
evidence: Providers and deployers of other AI systems and models and deployers of high-risk AI systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data

question: Can a high-risk AI system in a product covered by the Union harmonisation legislation in Section B of Annex I be tested in real-world conditions outside an AI regulatory sandbox?
reference: Yes, where the Member State allows it. Under Article 60a, Member States may allow such testing by providers or prospective providers of AI-enabled products covered by Section B of Annex I, must adopt real-world testing frameworks and notify them to the Commission before implementing them, and the frameworks must include a mandatory real-world testing plan.
probe: new Article 60a; in the original, Article 2(2) did not make the testing rules apply to Section B products
evidence: Member States may allow, in accordance with this Article, the testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes by providers or prospective providers of AI enabled products covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section B of Annex I

question: Does an AI system in a product that is used only for user assistance or performance optimisation count as a safety component?
reference: No. Article 6(1a) states that AI systems solely used for non-safety related aspects of user assistance, performance optimisation, service efficiency, automation or convenience or quality control do not qualify as safety components. Under Article 6(1b), a system whose failure or malfunctioning would endanger health and safety still does.
evidence: solely used for non-safety related aspects of user assistance, performance optimisation, service efficiency, automation or convenience or quality control shall not qualify as safety components

question: By when must providers of generative AI systems that were placed on the market before 2 August 2026 comply with the machine-readable marking obligation in Article 50(2)?
probe: new transitional rule; the original has none for Article 50(2)
evidence: that have been placed on the market before 2 August 2026 shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026

question: For a small mid-cap enterprise, is an administrative fine under Article 99(4) or (5) capped at the percentage of turnover or at the fixed amount?
reference: Whichever is lower. Article 99(6a) states that in the case of SMCs each fine referred to in paragraphs 4 and 5 is up to the percentages or amount referred to there, whichever is lower.
probe: the original only gives the lower cap to SMEs; for anyone else it is whichever is higher
evidence: In the case of SMCs, each fine referred to in paragraphs 4 and 5 shall be up to the percentages or amount referred therein, whichever is lower.

question: A small mid-cap enterprise provides an AI system for recruitment that is listed in Annex III. From when must it meet the high-risk requirements, and can it provide the Annex IV technical documentation in a simplified form?
reference: From 2 December 2027 under Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i). Yes: under Article 11(1), SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs may provide the Annex IV elements in a simplified manner, using the simplified technical documentation form the Commission establishes.
probe: two amended provisions; the original gives 2 August 2026 and limits the simplified form to SMEs
evidence: 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III
SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs, may provide the elements of the technical documentation specified in Annex IV in a simplified manner
